article_title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Scientific Visualization Literacy
citation: Patrick Phuoc Do, Chau M. Ta, Chaoli Wang. (2026). Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Scientific Visualization Literacy. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15176v2
title: SVLAT: Scientific Visualization Literacy Assessment Test
description: SVLAT is a standardized, psychometrically grounded instrument for measuring how well non-experts read, understand, and interpret scientific visualizations and illustrations. It "consists of 49 items based on 18 scientific visualizations and illustrations, including static images and animations, spanning 8 SciVis techniques and 11 task types." It follows a closed-world design in which each item is intended to be answerable using only the provided visualization and caption. In this article it serves as the benchmark for evaluating MLLM SciVis literacy, with a human baseline established via an online tryout with 485 non-expert participants.
requirements: Items are answered under a closed-world design using only the provided visualization and caption, limiting reliance on external knowledge.
constraints: Some tasks are represented by only one or two items, which limits the reliability of per-task estimates.
target_learning_goals: reading, understanding, and interpreting scientific visualizations and illustrations
examples: Used to benchmark three closed-source and three open-source MLLMs against a human baseline of 485 participants.
key_sources: Patrick Phuoc Do, Chau M. Ta, Chaoli Wang. (2026). Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Scientific Visualization Literacy. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15176

article_title: High-intensity acute exercise impacts motor learning in healthy older adults
citation: Eleanor M. Taylor, Claire J. Cadwallader, Dylan Curtin, Trevor T.-J. Chong, Joshua J. Hendrikse & James P. Coxon. (2024). High-intensity acute exercise impacts motor learning in healthy older adults. npj Science of Learning 9:9. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00220-2
title: Cognitively demanding variant of the sequential visual isometric pinch task (SVIPT) with three sequences
description: A computer-based force pinch task in which participants squeeze a transducer to move a cursor to five coloured targets in a specified sequence, with target orders pseudorandomly shuffled among 3 different orders. The article describes it as "a more cognitively challenging version of the SVIPT that requires the trial-to-trial recall, planning, execution, and learning of multiple sequences," engaging both explicit sequence learning and implicit force-to-cursor mapping. Skill was scored via a speed-accuracy trade-off function.
requirements: A force transducer, on-screen cursor display, and per-block skill feedback to encourage improvement
constraints: Force target set at 45% of each participant's maximum voluntary pinch contraction; retention tested same-day after a 6-hour delay without sleep
target_learning_goals: explicit and implicit motor sequence learning
examples: 10 blocks of 12 acquisition trials, then a warm-up and four retention blocks after the delay
key_sources: Eleanor M. Taylor, Claire J. Cadwallader, Dylan Curtin, Trevor T.-J. Chong, Joshua J. Hendrikse & James P. Coxon. (2024). High-intensity acute exercise impacts motor learning in healthy older adults. npj Science of Learning 9:9. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00220-2

article_title: Actualization of teaching conceptions in lesson design: how teaching conceptions shape TPACK regarding spherical video-based virtual reality-supported writing instruction
citation: Mengyuan Chen, Ching-sing Chai, Morris Siu-Yung Jong. (2023). Actualization of teaching conceptions in lesson design: how teaching conceptions shape TPACK regarding spherical video-based virtual reality-supported writing instruction. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-023-10295-0
title: SVVR-supported writing learning system built with EduVenture VR
description: The SVVR learning system used in the study was developed with EduVenture VR, which, as the article states, "consists of an SVVR composer for teachers and a user interface for students". Teachers filmed local Hong Kong places with a panoramic camera and built SVVR environments in the composer, adding human-computer interactions such as voice prompts, tags, portals, single/multiple-choice questions, and voice memos to guide students' exploration and stimulate thinking. The system immersed students in an authentic field trip experience for writing.
requirements: Teachers use the SVVR composer to film places with a panoramic camera and edit videos with interactive elements
constraints: Images are filmed in the real world and viewed through a simple headset such as Google cardboard glasses
examples: Each teaching unit lasted 14-18 periods (45 minutes each): eight to ten periods of reading comprehension, four to six periods of SVVR-assisted writing, and two periods of evaluation and feedback
key_sources: Mengyuan Chen, Ching-sing Chai, Morris Siu-Yung Jong. (2023). Actualization of teaching conceptions in lesson design: how teaching conceptions shape TPACK regarding spherical video-based virtual reality-supported writing instruction. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-023-10295-0

article_title: Learning in serious virtual worlds: Evaluation of learning effectiveness and appeal to students in the E-Junior project
citation: Wrzesien, M., & Alcañiz Raya, M. (2010). Learning in serious virtual worlds: Evaluation of learning effectiveness and appeal to students in the E-Junior project. In Computers & Education (Vol. 55, Issue 1, pp. 178–187). Elsevier BV. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2010.01.003
title: Serious virtual worlds as a class format matched to traditional classes with identical learning objectives and contents
description: The study's evaluation pattern holds content constant while varying the class format: a virtual group learned in a serious virtual world while a traditional group received "a traditional type of class that contained identical learning objectives and contents but lacked a gaming aspect." This design isolates the gaming/virtual-world aspect as the difference between conditions. It was applied to elementary natural science and ecology content about the Mediterranean Sea.
requirements: The two class formats must contain identical learning objectives and contents
examples: E-Junior evaluation: 48 children assigned to a serious-virtual-world class versus a traditional class with the same objectives and content
key_sources: Wrzesien, M., & Alcañiz Raya, M. (2010). Learning in serious virtual worlds: Evaluation of learning effectiveness and appeal to students in the E-Junior project. In Computers & Education (Vol. 55, Issue 1, pp. 178–187). Elsevier BV. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2010.01.003

article_title: The Effects of the Comprehensive Inductive Educational Approach on the Social Behaviour of Preschool Children in Kindergarten
citation: Robi Kroflič and Helena Smrtnik Vitulić. (2015). The Effects of the Comprehensive Inductive Educational Approach on the Social Behaviour of Preschool Children in Kindergarten. c e p s Journal, Vol.5, No1. https://journals.cepsj.si/index.php/cepsj
title: SV-O questionnaire (Slovenian version of the Social Competence and Behaviour Evaluation questionnaire)
description: The SV-O is a Slovenian-normed teacher-rating instrument for evaluating individual children's social behaviour in educational institutions. "The SV-O questionnaire consists of 80 statements about the child's behaviour rated on a 6-point scale", combined into eight basic scales covering emotional adaptation, peer interaction and interaction with adults, and into four composite scales including Social Competence and General Adaptation. T values between 38T and 62T represent an average result. In this study internal reliability ranged from 0.85 to 0.93 for basic scales.
requirements: Designed for completion by kindergarten teachers or first-year primary teachers who know the children well and interact with them daily in the educational institution
constraints: The article states the SV-O was insufficient for providing exact evidence of the different developmental processes fostered by the CIEA
target_learners: children older than 2.5 years in kindergarten and first-grade primary school
target_learning_goals: evaluating children's social competence, internalising and externalising problems, and general social adaptation
examples: Used as pre-test and post-test in the quasi-experiment, with eight kindergarten teachers rating the 52 EG children and nine rating the 48 CG children
key_sources: Robi Kroflič and Helena Smrtnik Vitulić. (2015). The Effects of the Comprehensive Inductive Educational Approach on the Social Behaviour of Preschool Children in Kindergarten. c e p s Journal, Vol.5, No1. https://journals.cepsj.si/index.php/cepsj

article_title: Spherical Video-Based Virtual Reality Training for Nurses' Delirium Care Competence: A Randomized Controlled Trial With Qualitative Evaluation.
citation: Hung Yin-Ling, Zhou Yi-Chao, Feng Hsin-Pei, Lin Chia-Huei, Chien Wu-Chien, Tzeng Wen-Chii. (2026). Spherical Video‐Based Virtual Reality Training for Nurses’ Delirium Care Competence: A Randomized Controlled Trial With Qualitative Evaluation. Journal of Nursing Management. https://doi.org/10.1155/jonm/8355655
title: SVVR delirium care training program: four interactive 360° modules grounded in Bandura's self-efficacy theory
description: The program comprises four modules covering delirium assessment, safety measure analysis, risk factor identification and management, and interprofessional holistic care, delivered as a single 15-minute session via a head-mounted display with 10 embedded interactive questions answered by spoken response. Each module "included components of Bandura's self-efficacy theory, including vicarious learning, simulated mastery experiences, and verbal encouragement". Content validity from a five-member expert panel yielded a scale-level content validity index of 0.92, and the program was pilot-tested with 10 nurses before the trial.
requirements: Delivered individually in a private simulation room following a standardized protocol, with fast-forwarding and skipping disabled
Mandarin Chinese speech recognition technology to capture spoken responses to embedded questions
constraints: Image resolution, speech recognition capture, and equipment adjustments (near-sightedness, astigmatism, presbyopia) were reported by participants as areas needing improvement
target_learners: Registered nurses caring for acutely ill patients at risk of delirium
target_learning_goals: Safety measures and risk factor management
examples: Videos were captured in vacant private ICUs and conference rooms using an Insta360 X3 camera, with roles played by consenting hospital nursing staff
key_sources: Hung Yin-Ling, Zhou Yi-Chao, Feng Hsin-Pei, Lin Chia-Huei, Chien Wu-Chien, Tzeng Wen-Chii. (2026). Spherical Video‐Based Virtual Reality Training for Nurses’ Delirium Care Competence: A Randomized Controlled Trial With Qualitative Evaluation. Journal of Nursing Management. https://doi.org/10.1155/jonm/8355655

article_title: [Evaluation of a training model for health professionals in the care of critical patients: AIPCAP Study].
citation: Cánovas Zaldúa Y., Casabella Abril B., Martín Cantera C., González García F., Moreno Escribá S., del Val García J.L. (2020). Evaluación de un modelo formativo para profesionales sanitarios en la atención del paciente crítico: Estudio AIPCAP. Atencion Primaria. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aprim.2018.08.009
title: ABCDE immediate life support methodology for structured assessment of the critical patient
description: The article's training rests on immediate life support (SVI) organised as the A-B-C-D-E methodology: "A (airway/vía aérea) – B (breathing/respiración) – C (circulation/circulación) – D (disability/neurológico) – E (exposure/exposición)". Every critical patient should be treated following these stages "en estricto orden, y no iniciar ninguna etapa sin haber valorado la anterior". The AIPCAP checklist operationalises this framework into 7 stages (adding first look and additional information) for structured evaluation and feedback during simulated emergencies.
requirements: The strict sequential order of stages must be followed, with no stage started before the previous one is assessed
target_learners: Health professionals in primary care attending medical emergencies
target_learning_goals: Structured, expert initial assessment and stabilisation of critically ill patients before hospital transfer
examples: The AIPCAP training sessions opened with an explanation of the A-B-C-D-E methodology before rescuers queried clinical parameters of the simulated case
key_sources: Cánovas Zaldúa Y., Casabella Abril B., Martín Cantera C., González García F., Moreno Escribá S., del Val García J.L. (2020). Evaluación de un modelo formativo para profesionales sanitarios en la atención del paciente crítico: Estudio AIPCAP. Atencion Primaria. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aprim.2018.08.009
